topic: why Costco has sold its hot dog and soda for one dollar fifty since the mid 1980s and will not raise it
storyAngle: The hot dog is a loss leader that keeps people walking in; the real money is the membership card.
doNotClaim: Do not say what Costco earns or loses on the combo; no source gives that. Analysts call it a loss leader, Costco has not published its margin.
Do not use vague money words like "a few cents" or "pennies".
Do not give an exact launch year; sources say only "mid-1980s".
Do not quote profanity or violence; paraphrase the founder anecdote and say "reportedly".

facts.claim: The Costco hot dog and soda combo costs $1.50 and has since the mid-1980s.
Costco sold nearly 200 million combos in fiscal 2023.
Costco began running its own hot dog factories in 2008 to cut supply-chain costs.
Reportedly, co-founder Jim Sinegal told then-CEO Craig Jelinek not to raise the price (a 2018 interview; the article calls the story part legend). Paraphrase it, say "reportedly".

Analysts describe the combo as loss-leader pricing; Forrester analyst Brendan Witcher said "The retailer is ultimately eating that cost to keep the customer loyal." Costco itself has not published a margin for the combo.
facts.note: attribute to analysts; do not state a Costco margin

facts.claim: Costco FY2024 MEMBERSHIP FEE REVENUE (what members paid in annual fees) was $4,828 million.
Costco FY2024 OPERATING INCOME (profit from operations) was $9,285 million.
Annual fees rose on Sept 1 2024: Gold Star/Business from $60 to $65, Executive from $120 to $130.

derived.claim: Membership fee revenue was about 52% of Costco operating income (4,828 / 9,285): about half.
